chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony of children, when they are called as witnesses while they are young, is valid when they grow up, provided they have not forgotten it.'

key_terms.أَشْهَدُوهُمْ: When they are called as witnesses

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a child valid in Islamic law if they remember it as an adult?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the legal principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) regarding the testimony of children, affirming that their early witness remains binding upon adulthood provided they retain the memory. It highlights the Shia juristic view that childhood is not a barrier to legal competence in witnessing, provided the cognitive capacity to remember is preserved, a nuance often discussed in *usul al-fiqh* debates concerning the age of discernment (*mumayyiz*).
